report.summary: Chunk 3 of 4 of shape.py: continues the describe() function with table, tree, dict, dataclass, sequence, scalar, and opaque branches, then defines ShapeConflict dataclass and its to_dict method.
risks: lines 241-247 | medium | The code catches generic Exception when extracting dims from shape attribute; any non-integer or failure silently yields empty tuple. This could hide type errors or malformed shapes. | Confirm whether catching specific exceptions (TypeError, ValueError) is sufficient and whether silent fallback is intended.

lines 249-256 | medium | Similar generic Exception catch when computing dtypes; if dtypes attribute exists but conversion to string fails, dtype string becomes empty. | Check if specific exceptions like TypeError should be caught instead of all.

lines 257-263 | medium | memory_usage(deep=False) may raise AttributeError if obj is not a DataFrame; the fallback to nbytes might not be equivalent. | Verify that the fallback is appropriate for all table-like objects.

lines 267-280 | medium | The tree branch uses generic Exception when listing keys; any failure results in empty names. This could mask important errors (e.g., permission denied). | Consider catching specific exceptions like OSError or TypeError.

lines 283-290 | medium | Dict branch: uses next(iter(obj.values())) without ordering guarantee; if dict is large, this is fine but note that element is taken from first item only. | No action needed, but document that element is from arbitrary first value.

lines 292-302 | medium | Dataclass and __slots__ branches: does not probe element types or values; only returns field names. This is a design choice but could miss nesting. | No action needed if design intent is to only record field names.
lines 304-310 | medium | Sequence branch: probes one element via next(iter(obj)); for set/frozenset, order is arbitrary. | Document that element is from arbitrary first element.
lines 312-316 | medium | String/bytes branch: only records length, no content. | No action needed by design.
lines 318-320 | medium | Scalar branch: no note, no length. | No action needed.
lines 322-323 | medium | Opaque branch: returns note that shape could not be characterised. | No action needed.

line 330 | medium | ShapeConflict docstring claims missing_in_observation is softest signal and undeclared_in_observation is sharpest. This is a design claim, not directly checkable in code. | Check that calling code treats these fields accordingly.
todos: Review generic Exception catches in dims, dtypes, memory_usage, and tree branches; consider narrowing to specific exceptions.
Ensure that the dict branch's element probe (first value) is documented as arbitrary.
Verify that ShapeConflict.agrees property logic matches documented intent: agrees when comparable and no undeclared fields.

claims.text: missing_in_observation is the softest signal — these inputs did not exercise that field.
claims.why: The claim about the semantics of the field is not checkable from the code in this chunk; it depends on how the field is populated and used elsewhere.

claims.text: undeclared_in_observation is the sharp one: the object carries something the code never declared, so the declaration is incomplete or the payload has undocumented shape.
claims.why: The claim about the severity of undeclared fields is not checkable from this chunk; it depends on usage in other code.

claims.text: agrees property: returns True if comparable and no undeclared fields.
claims.why: The property returns `self.comparable and not self.undeclared_in_observation`, which matches the claim.

observations.what: Generic Exception catches in dims, dtypes, memory_usage, and tree branches may hide errors.
Dict branch probes first value without guaranteeing order; element is from arbitrary key.
Sequence branch probes one element via next(iter(obj)); for sets/frozensets order is arbitrary.
ShapeConflict docstring makes claims about field semantics that are not verifiable in this chunk.
